title: Qualitative Analysis Flowchart
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Interactive Mermaid flowchart of the classical cation separation scheme. Students step through four precipitating reagents and five analytical groups, or choose one of 18 cations and trace where it precipitates, with net ionic equations and precipitate colors in a side panel.

learningObjectives: Explain how a mixture of cations is separated into groups by adding precipitating reagents in a fixed order
Classify a cation into its analytical group and predict the precipitate it forms
Explain why the order of the reagents matters
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 4: Chemical Reactions (net ionic equations, precipitation)

controls.label: Trace a cation
controls.description: Chooses one of 18 cations to follow through the scheme, or None to show every step

controls.label: Previous
controls.description: Moves back one box along the current path

controls.label: Next
controls.description: Moves forward one box along the current path

assumptions: Groups and ions are those listed in the chapter text
Separations are treated as complete; in practice some PbCl2 stays dissolved and carries into Group II

keyQuestions: Which anion does the precipitating at each step?
Why must the chlorides be removed before sulfide is added?
Why is ammonium tested on a fresh sample?
commonMisconceptions: Believing the reagents can be added in any order
Believing a white precipitate identifies a single ion
Forgetting that ions not precipitated remain in the filtrate
assessmentOpportunities: Give a set of observations and have students identify the ion and write the net ionic equation
